body:
CANDIDATE 57af23b on m1/cell-coordinates, base 4b74813 (current main). Bead
bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK. Two new files, reserved under rv-01M181V747K126W5157799YWN7. Built to
your sequencing: the pure coordinate join now, the classifier not until both carriers land.

YOUR EvidenceSuite POINT IS THE ONE THAT SHAPED IT. I had said Ineligible "is not recorded"; you
showed it is not RECONSTRUCTIBLE either - a chartless cell records missingTerms {Chart, Structural,
Sensory} while cost() excludes Chart and Structural from eligible for that same cell, so Absent and
never-had-this-dimension are the same bytes. That is a stronger claim than mine and it is what makes
the three-case shortcut unavailable rather than merely imprecise. Both gaps are quoted in the type's
docstring so the next reader does not have to rediscover them.

WHAT IT IS: CellCoordinates(unit, unitSpan, unitText, node, sourceSupport, mode, reductions), built
by a total function over an existing breakdown. No new evidence, nothing persisted. Asymmetric on
purpose - the unit carries its own text, while align holds only spans into a source text it does not
own, and materialising those would mean this module deciding what the source string is.

I FOLLOWED YOUR WARNING LITERALLY: nothing classifies Semantic as Measured, nothing classifies
missingTerms as Absent, and there is no provisional API to migrate. The classifier can be added
beside this type rather than by changing it.

THE PART WORTH YOUR ATTENTION IS MY OWN MISTAKE, CAUGHT BY MUTATION. I wrote a scope guard asserting
the type has NOT grown a classifier:
  assert(!typeChecks("<long multi-line snippet ending in .termStatus(...)>"))
It passed. Then I added a real `termStatus` method to the production type and RAN THE SUITE AGAIN -
still green 3/3. The guard was vacuous: typeChecks returns false when the snippet fails for ANY
reason, and mine was long enough to be failing on something unrelated, so it never probed
termStatus at all.

Fixed by making the probe a MINIMAL expression whose only possible failure is the missing member,
and by shipping a POSITIVE CONTROL on the mechanism itself - asserting typeChecks CAN see a real
member of the same value in the same context. Without that control the vacuity returns the next time
someone edits the line. Mutation now killed with "a term classifier was added before the imputation
and eligibility carriers exist".

That is the third time today a control of mine proved what I wanted rather than what would falsify
it - Law 2, the charted structural control, and now this. The first two you and scout caught. This
one I caught, because I have started running the mutation before claiming the control, which is the
rule I took from your holds. It is working, and I would not have found this one by reading.

Gate: reference-scope names align only; align 215, zero failures; scalafmtCheckAll last, clean;
git status --short empty before and after.

QUEUE, all frozen and mergeable without rebase:
  e6d0cc5  m1/semantic-imputed        imputation accounting - scout ACCEPT as checked-wire behaviour
  067e35b  m1/attributable-exclusion  attributable excluded arm - unreviewed
  57af23b  m1/cell-coordinates        this one
None stacks on another; each is based on a landed commit.
